IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-generated UUID idempotency key. Duplicate request with the same key
and the same request payload within 72h returns the stored response without
re-execution. Reusing the same key with different request parameters returns
an idempotency conflict.
Scope: (tenant_id, key). UUID v7 is recommended.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

ServiceUnavailable.description:
A required Arc Pay dependency is temporarily unavailable.

The response body uses `error.type=api_error` and
`error.code=service_unavailable`. Treat this as transient: retry with
exponential backoff and jitter, keep the same `Idempotency-Key` for mutating
requests, and poll `GET /payments/{id}` before retrying a payment operation
when the client did not receive a definitive response.

Timeout.description:
Arc Pay did not receive a definitive downstream response before the public
API deadline.

The response body uses `error.type=api_error` and `error.code=timeout`.
Treat this as pending confirmation, not a decline: keep the same order in a
waiting state, poll `GET /payments/{id}`, and wait for the webhook or
reconciliation result. Do not repeat the payment with a new idempotency key
unless the original payment reaches a terminal failed/declined state.

available-payment-method.description:
Merchant-visible method/mode pair for the authenticated key environment.
Missing pairs are not enabled for this shop configuration and must not be
rendered. Optional constraint fields are advisory; final currency, amount,
country, terminal, and bank-limit validation happens when creating the
payment, checkout session, or payment link.

is_active.description: Availability flag for this method/mode pair.

max_amount.description: Maximum amount in minor units when advertised for this pair.

min_amount.description: Minimum amount in minor units when advertised for this pair.

sandbox_requirements.description: Method-specific sandbox enablement notes, credentials, or test scenario prerequisites.

supported_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 buyer or issuer countries advertised for this pair when configured.

supported_currencies.description: Currencies currently advertised for this pair. If absent, validate by creating the payment.

unavailable_reason.description: Optional merchant-facing reason when a configured pair is visible but currently unavailable.

capture-mode.description:
Payment capture stage mode. `one_stage` authorizes and captures in one bank
operation. `two_stage` authorizes funds first; capture or void happens later.
For `payment_method=sbp`, the effective payment capture mode is always
`one_stage`; if a checkout session or payment link also allows card payments,
`two_stage` applies only when the buyer selects a card/card-like method that
supports authorization followed by capture.

amount.description:
Amount to capture in minor units. Must be <= authorized amount.
If omitted, captures the full authorized amount.
Partial capture auto-voids the remaining authorized amount.

customer_email.description: Buyer email for bank fiscal receipts. Required with fiscal_items when customer_phone is empty.

customer_id.description: Merchant customer identifier used when the card token was created.

customer_phone.description: Buyer phone for bank fiscal receipts. Required with fiscal_items when customer_email is empty.

external_id.description: Merchant order reference. Must be unique per organization.

item_code.description: Bank fiscal item code required for embedded fiscal receipts.

merchant_inn.description: Merchant or organization INN used as FFD company INN. Required when fiscal_items is non-empty.

recurring_expiry.description: Optional recurring authorization expiry date in YYYYMMDD format.

stored_credential_reason.description: Merchant-initiated transaction reason for stored credential framework. Omit for unscheduled COF.

url.description: Hosted checkout URL where the buyer completes payment.

browser_info.description: Browser fingerprint for 3DS 2.x finalization. Customer IP is server-detected and must not be supplied in the JSON body.

completion_indicator.description:
Y = method loaded successfully, N = browser does not support,
U = method timed out or unknown result.

callback_url.description: Optional webhook endpoint for this setup payment lifecycle.

customer_id.description: Merchant's stable customer identifier that owns the saved card consent.

external_id.description: Optional merchant reference for this setup attempt.

fail_url.description: HTTPS browser return URL after failed authentication.

success_url.description: HTTPS browser return URL after successful authentication.

create-checkout-session-request.description:
Creates a hosted checkout session. `payment_methods` must use method/mode
pairs returned by `GET /payment-methods/available` for the same API key
environment and shop configuration. `success_url`, `fail_url`, and
`cancel_url` must be HTTPS URLs.

autocompletion_date.description:
Optional bank-side auto-capture time for card two-stage payments. Ignored
for SBP payments created from mixed card + SBP sessions.

customer_id.description: Merchant's stable customer identifier for card-on-file consent and lookup. Required when the session can save a card.

item_code.description: Bank fiscal item code required for embedded fiscal receipts.

return_url.description: Optional URL where the bank/app can return the buyer after SBP flow.

external_sale_id.description: Merchant POS receipt/order identifier for idempotent lookup.

organization_id.description:
Shop scope. Secret API keys are organization-scoped; omitting this value
uses the organization bound to the key. Supplying a different organization
returns 403.

create-link-request.description:
Creates one-time, reusable, invoice, or recurring payment links.
Conditional rules enforced at runtime:
- `link_type=invoice` requires at least one `items[]` entry.
- `link_type=recurring` requires `billing_config`, `customer_id`, and `capture_mode=one_stage`.
- `redirect_url` and `webhook_url` must be HTTPS URLs.

amount.description: Amount in minor units. For reusable links, 0 lets the buyer enter the amount.

autocompletion_date.description:
Optional bank-side auto-capture time for card two-stage payments. Ignored
for SBP payments created from mixed card + SBP links.

customer_id.description: Merchant's stable customer identifier. Required for recurring links so card tokens can be saved and billed later.

environment.description: Must match the API key environment when provided.

items.description: Required when `link_type=invoice`; ignored for non-invoice links.

item_code.description: Bank fiscal item code required for embedded fiscal receipts.

payment_mode.description: Merchant-facing mode for this method. Arc Pay maps the method/mode pair to the internal route configured for the shop.

redirect_url.description:
Single return URL used after hosted payment-link flow completion,
cancellation, or pending handoff. Do not infer final payment state from
this URL alone; use `webhook_url`, the payment webhook, or
`GET /payments/{id}`.

webhook_url.description: Webhook endpoint for payment events created from this link.

amount.description: Amount in minor units (kopecks for RUB, tiyn for KZT, tiyin for UZS).

callback_url.description:
Webhook endpoint for async payment status events for this payment. Arc Pay
sends events for created, pending 3DS, authorization/capture, decline,
failure, timeout, refund, void, expiry, and chargeback transitions when
delivery is configured. Synchronous execution failures still return in the
API response; if a terminal payment record exists, a matching status event
is also eligible for delivery.

customer_id.description: Merchant's stable customer identifier for customer-scoped payment flows. Card-on-file setup uses `POST /cards/setup`.

external_id.description: Merchant order reference. Must be unique per organization.

fail_url.description:
Merchant browser return URL after failed card H2H/3DS authentication.
Required for `payment_method=bank_card`, and for `payment_method=tpay`
because T-Bank marks it mandatory. Optional for other wallet/APM methods
unless the selected bank adapter requires it.
Browser return is a UX signal only; final order confirmation must still
use webhook delivery or GET /payments/{id}.

item_code.description: Bank fiscal item code required for embedded fiscal receipts.

merchant_inn.description: Merchant or organization INN used as FFD company INN. Required when fiscal_items is non-empty.

return_url.description:
Single buyer return URL for wallet/APM methods such as `sbp`, `sberpay`,
`tpay`, and `alfapay`. Arc Pay forwards this URL to acquiring adapters
that need a bank-side `returnUrl`/`redirect_url`, and returns it as wallet
action metadata when available. Required for `payment_method=tpay` because
T-Bank marks it mandatory; for SBP it is required only when the selected
bank specification requires `returnUrl`.

split_execution_mode.description:
Marketplace split execution mode. Omit or send `auto` to select
bank-native split when the routed bank terminal supports it, otherwise
Arc Pay platform split. `bank_native` fails closed if the selected bank
cannot accept split instructions on authorization.

split_rules.description: Inline one-off split rules. Mutually exclusive with `split_template_id`.

value.description: Basis points for percent, minor units for fixed, zero for remainder.

split_template_id.description: Reusable split template identifier. Mutually exclusive with `split_rules`.

success_url.description:
Merchant browser return URL after successful card H2H/3DS authentication.
Required for `payment_method=bank_card`. Wallet/APM methods use
`return_url` when a bank-side buyer return URL is needed.
Browser return is a UX signal only; final order confirmation must still
use webhook delivery or GET /payments/{id}.

amount.description:
Amount to refund in minor units. Must be <= captured amount.
Multiple partial refunds are supported; total must not exceed captured amount.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable error code. `service_unavailable` means an Arc Pay
dependency is temporarily unavailable; retry with exponential backoff and
jitter, preserving the same idempotency key for mutating requests.
`fiscal_receipts_unavailable` means the payment was fiscalized in the
payment flow, but the bank/OFD provider has no receipt status for it.

decline_code.description: Canonical payment decline code when applicable.

param.description: Request parameter or field that caused the error.

request_id.description: Unique request identifier. Provide to support when reporting issues.

event-payment-authorized.description:
Emitted when the issuing bank approves the auth-hold on the
cardholder's funds. Funds are reserved but not yet captured.
Two-stage payments stay in AUTHORIZED until your capture call;
one-stage flows transition immediately to CAPTURED (you may
receive both events back-to-back).

bank_auth_code.description: Issuer authorization code for the original payment.

bank_internal_ref.description: Bank/acquirer internal reference for dispute matching.

bank_rrn.description: Retrieval Reference Number from the card network or bank registry.

event-payment-captured.description:
Emitted when the captured amount has been debited from the cardholder.
For one-stage payments this fires after a successful auth without a
separate capture call.

bank_auth_code.description: Issuer authorization code for the original payment.

bank_internal_ref.description: Bank/acquirer internal reference for dispute matching.

bank_rrn.description: Retrieval Reference Number from the card network or bank registry.

event-payment-chargeback.description:
Cardholder filed a dispute with their issuing bank. The disputed
amount is held from the next settlement until the dispute is
resolved. Worst-case dispute windows vary by network and reason code:
Visa and Mastercard can reach 540 days for some delayed-delivery or
services-not-received scenarios; Mir card disputes can reach 360 days;
SBP dispute handling can reach 540 days. See the Arc Pay chargeback
policy documentation for merchant-facing operating guidance.

event-payment-created.description:
Emitted when a payment record is first created via POST /payments,
before any bank interaction. The payment is in CREATED state.

event-payment-declined.description:
Bank-side decline (do_not_honor, insufficient_funds, restricted_card,
fraud_suspected, expired_card, etc.) or AML rule decline. The decline
reason is in `payment.decline_code`. Terminal — re-attempt requires a
new payment with a new idempotency key.

event-payment-expired.description:
Authorization-hold timed out before a capture was issued. Typical
auth window is 7 days; varies per bank. Funds are returned to the
cardholder automatically — no merchant action required.

event-payment-failed.description:
Internal or upstream error preventing the payment from completing.
Distinct from declined — failed indicates Arc Pay or the bank could
not reach a definitive decision before final timeout. Terminal.

event-payment-refunded.description:
Funds returned to the cardholder. Partial refunds are supported up
to the captured amount; this event fires once per refund operation,
not once per payment. payment.captured_amount and payment.refunded_amount
update accordingly.

event-payment-settled.description:
Emitted when a captured payment is included in a settlement batch.
This is an operations/accounting signal, not a buyer-facing payment result.

event-payment-timeout.description:
Bank did not respond within Arc Pay's outbound timeout window. NOT
a terminal state — the bank may still confirm asynchronously, in
which case payment.captured or payment.failed follows. Do NOT
cancel the order on timeout.

event-payment-voided.description:
Authorization-hold released without capture, typically because the
merchant called POST /payments/{id}/void before capture, or
partial capture left a remainder that auto-voids.

browser_info.description: Browser fingerprint for card 3DS 2.x device identification. Required only for `bank_card + h2h`. Customer IP is server-detected and must not be supplied in the JSON body.

card_token_id.description: Token returned by /tokenize. Required only for `bank_card + h2h`.

payment_mode.description: Merchant-facing payment mode. For this endpoint it must be `h2h`; use hosted payment links/HPP for `redirect`.

wallet_interaction.description:
Explicit wallet/APM interaction requested by a merchant-hosted H2H form.
Required for wallet/APM methods such as `sbp + h2h` and `sberpay + h2h`.
`provider` must match `payment_method`.

action.description: Requested buyer interaction for this wallet/APM execution.

app_deep_link.description: Merchant app deep link used by native mobile integrations.

back_url.description: Merchant return URL for wallet app or bank page handoff.

phone.description: Buyer phone for phone-push wallet flows when the provider requires it.

surface.description: Merchant-controlled buyer surface that will render the next action.

authorized_amount.description: Amount placed on hold (kopecks). Populated for two-stage payments.

card_token_id.description:
Reusable saved-card token returned only when this execution completed a
card setup and the bank returned a real reusable binding/rebill
identifier.

liability_shifted.description: True when 3DS liability shift was achieved.

amount.description: Amount in minor units for the given ISO 4217 currency.

refund_id.description: Stable refund identifier for reconciliation and idempotent retries.

exchange_rate.description: Decimal exchange rate snapshot used for this sale.

barcode.description:
Existing catalog barcode. Supplying this field makes the line a catalog
lookup. Omit it for manual ad hoc line items.

name.description:
Display name for manual ad hoc line items. For catalog lines, the stored
catalog product name is authoritative.

sku.description:
Existing catalog SKU. When `sku`, `barcode`, or `product_id` is supplied
by the API client, Arc Pay resolves the line from the imported Foreign POS
catalog and uses the catalog product name, price, currency, and version as
the authoritative sale snapshot. Omit catalog identifiers for an ad hoc
manual line priced only by `name` and `unit_price`.

local_currency.description: Currency used for catalog prices at the overseas POS location.

payment_currency.description: Currency charged to the customer through the configured payment method.

settlement_currency.description: Currency credited to the merchant settlement ledger.

organization_id.description: Optional explicit organization guard. Must match the API key organization.

autocompletion_date.description: Bank-side auto-capture time for card two-stage payments.

customer_id.description: Merchant's stable customer identifier used for recurring card-on-file links.

redirect_url.description:
Single merchant return URL for hosted link outcomes. Success, failure,
cancellation, and pending flows all return through this URL; confirm final
state via webhook or payment lookup.

webhook_url.description: Webhook endpoint used for payments created from this link.

amount.description: Amount in minor units (kopecks for RUB, tiyn for KZT, tiyin for UZS).
Amount in minor units. Zero is used only for card setup intents.

authorized_amount.description: Amount authorized by the bank in minor units.

bank_auth_code.description: Authorization code returned by the bank.

bank_code.description:
Opaque acquiring route code used for support and reconciliation. Treat it
as metadata, not as a payment-flow switch.

bank_internal_ref.description: Opaque acquirer/provider internal reference for reconciliation.

bank_order_id.description: Opaque acquirer/provider order reference when separate from `bank_payment_id`.

bank_payment_id.description:
Opaque acquirer/provider payment reference for support, reconciliation, and
lifecycle correlation. Do not branch integration logic on its format.

bank_rrn.description: Retrieval Reference Number returned by the payment network.

bank_terminal_id.description:
Opaque acquiring terminal reference used for support and reconciliation.
Merchants do not need it to render SBP, wallet, or card next actions.

card_mask.description: Masked card PAN, first 6 and last 4 digits only.

card_token_id.description:
Saved card token produced by `POST /cards/setup`, or the saved-card token
used for a merchant-initiated card-on-file charge.

decline_code.description: Canonical decline code when the payment is declined or failed.

operations.description:
Merchant-safe immutable operation ledger summary for this payment. Internal
idempotency keys, bank request idempotency keys, raw adapter payloads and
event details are intentionally not part of the public contract.

payment_mode.description: Set after Execute resolves the route. Empty for draft payments.

redirect_url.description:
Redirect-mode or bank-hosted start URL. H2H 3DS browser work is exposed
only through `next_action.three_ds.submit`; do not use this field for
3DS Method or Challenge handling.

status.description:
Canonical Arc Pay payment status. Terminal statuses are `authorized`,
`captured`, `settled`, `voided`, `expired`, `refunded`, `chargeback`,
`declined`, and `failed`. `created`, `pending`, `pending_3ds`, and
`timeout` are non-terminal; keep the order pending and wait for webhook
delivery or `GET /payments/{id}` polling.

payment-flow-mode.description:
Merchant-facing interaction mode. `h2h` means host-to-host execution via
Arc Pay JS SDK/Hosted Fields or a direct integration where the merchant
environment handles card data. `redirect` means the payer is sent to a hosted
or bank-controlled checkout surface.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; omitted or empty when there are no more results.

payment-method.description:
Canonical merchant-facing payment method.

`bank_card` covers card entry and saved-card flows. `sbp`, `sberpay`,
`tpay`, `alfapay`, and other bank wallets are wallet/APM methods that can be
exposed by any configured acquiring route, not only by the bank named in the
method. Use the returned payment mode to decide whether the buyer stays on
Arc Pay/HPP (`h2h`) or is handed to a provider-hosted page (`redirect`).
Wallet/APM flows return method-agnostic details in `wallet_action` on
hosted/HPP execution surfaces when an explicit next action is required.

Direct H2H execute supports `bank_card` with a card token and enabled wallet
methods such as `sbp` and `sberpay` with `wallet_interaction`.

type.description:
Bank-agnostic browser action required before the payment can progress.
When this field is absent on the payment response, no browser handoff is
currently required.

target.description: Use hidden_iframe for 3DS Method and browser for visible ACS challenge.

completion_endpoint.description: Arc Pay endpoint your backend calls after the method step completes.

phase.description: Device-fingerprinting method step or visible ACS challenge.

three_ds_server_trans_id.description: 3DS Server Transaction ID; send it to /complete-3ds-method only after a method step.

version.description: Protocol family for the next 3-D Secure browser action.

bank_auth_code.description: Authorization code returned by the bank for this operation.

bank_internal_ref.description: Bank-internal operation reference returned by the acquirer.

bank_operation_id.description: Bank-side operation identifier when the adapter returns one.

bank_rrn.description: Retrieval Reference Number returned by the bank network for this operation.

error_code.description: Canonical or bank error code for failed operations.

error_message.description: Merchant-safe failure message for failed operations.

operation_ref_id.description: Merchant-safe operation reference, such as a refund or capture identifier.

external_id.description: Bank-side external receipt identifier when provided.

native_status.description: Bank-native receipt status label corresponding to status_code.

ofd_receipt_url.description: Public OFD receipt URL when the bank/OFD returns one.

operation_id.description: Bank-side operation identifier that produced the receipt.

operation_type.description: Bank operation type, for example AUTHORIZATION or REFUND.

receipt_type.description: Fiscal receipt type, for example sell or sell_refund.

bank_code.description: Acquiring adapter that owns the saved bank binding.

card_mask.description: Masked PAN display value. Full PAN is never returned.

card_scheme.description: Payment card scheme returned by the acquiring route/card vault.

card_token_id.description: Opaque saved-card credential token for card-on-file charges.

is_active.description: False after soft-delete or bank-side deactivation.

last_used_at.description: Last successful use time when available.

cvv.description: Card verification value. Never stored per PCI DSS Req 3.3.1.

pan.description: Card number. Must pass Luhn check (validated server-side).

card_bin.description: First 8 digits of PAN (ISO/IEC 7812-1:2017 extended BIN).

card_scheme.description: Card network identifier. Arc Pay returns `MC` for Mastercard.

reason.description: Optional void reason for audit purposes.

wallet-action.description:
Typed wallet/APM next action returned for methods such as SberPay, SBP,
T-Pay, AlfaPay, and other bank wallets. The action is method-agnostic: the
provider identifies the selected payment method, and action-specific fields
tell the HPP, SDK, or merchant form what to render next.

action.description:
Next interaction type. `redirect` opens a bank/provider page, `deeplink`
opens a mobile banking app, `qr` renders a QR payment handoff, `sdk`
starts a provider SDK, and `phone_push` asks the buyer to approve a push
or SMS flow in the banking app.

back_url.description: URL the wallet app or bank page should use to return the buyer.

bank_invoice_id.description:
Optional opaque provider reference associated with this wallet action.
Treat it as diagnostic metadata only; integrations must branch on
`provider`, `action`, and the renderable URL/QR fields.

params.description: Provider-specific render metadata. Treat keys as opaque hints, not as stable routing fields.

qr_content_type.description: MIME type of `qr_image_base64` when a QR image is returned.

qr_image_base64.description:
Optional base64-encoded QR image for QR-based wallet/APM actions. Render it
as an image when `qr_url` is absent; do not infer the acquiring bank or QR
provider from the payload shape.

qr_url.description: QR payload URL or page URL when the wallet action is QR-based.

url.description: Redirect, deeplink, or SDK bootstrap URL when returned by the bank.

data.description:
Event-specific payload in snake_case. Always includes payment_id. Known
event types use closed schemas; fields are added only through a versioned
contract update. Use GET /payments/{id} when you need the current full
Payment resource.

event_id.description: Deduplicate on this field — Arc Pay guarantees at-least-once delivery.

event_type.description:
WARNING: payment.timeout is NOT a terminal state. The bank may have
processed the payment. Do NOT cancel the order on timeout — wait for
payment.captured or payment.failed from reconciliation callbacks.

livemode.description: true for live events, false for sandbox events.

tenant_id.description: Merchant tenant that owns the event.

BearerApiKey.description:
API key in Authorization header.
Secret API keys use environment-specific prefixes documented in the API key
management guide.
Example: Authorization: Bearer <secret-api-key>

PublishableApiKey.description:
Publishable API key (pk_live_* or pk_test_*). May be exposed in browser
JavaScript only for tokenization endpoints. All server-side financial
operations require a secret key.
PublishableApiKey.name: X-Api-Key

PublishableBearerApiKey.description:
Publishable API key in the Authorization header.
Example: Authorization: Bearer <publishable-api-key>

info.description:
Arc Pay public REST API.

Version policy:

- `/v1` is the stable public API base path.
- `/openapi.yaml` and `/openapi.json` always publish the latest `/v1`
  contract.
- Generated clients should pin a downloaded OpenAPI file in CI and compare
  it with the published spec before upgrading.

Environment selection:

- Secret and publishable API key prefixes select the environment:
  `sk_test_*` / `pk_test_*` for sandbox, `sk_live_*` / `pk_live_*` for live.
- Endpoints that expose an `environment` parameter use it as an explicit
  guard and reject mismatches with the API key environment.
- Payment and checkout creation endpoints derive environment only from the
  authenticated key.

Availability:

Authenticated endpoints can return `503 service_unavailable` when a required
Arc Pay dependency, such as auth or routing, is down. Retry transient `503`
responses with exponential backoff and jitter. For mutating requests, reuse
the same `Idempotency-Key`; if a payment ID is already known, poll
`GET /payments/{id}` before retrying execution, capture, void, or refund.
info.title: Arc Pay API

get.description:
Returns reusable saved-card credentials for a merchant customer. The
response contains only non-sensitive display metadata and the opaque
`card_token_id` used by `POST /payments/saved-card`.

parameters.description: Merchant's stable customer identifier used when the card was saved.
parameters.name: customer_id

post.description:
Creates a zero-amount card setup intent for collecting customer consent
and obtaining a reusable `card_token_id` without charging the customer.

The public flow is bank-neutral:

1. `POST /cards/setup` creates a setup payment with `status=created`.
2. Tokenize the card with `POST /payments/{id}/tokenize`.
3. Execute with `POST /payments/{id}/execute`.
4. Complete `next_action.three_ds` exactly like a normal H2H card
   payment when 3DS Method or challenge is required.
5. Use the returned `card_token_id`, webhook payload, or
   `GET /payments/{id}` after terminal status.

Arc Pay returns `card_token_id` only after the selected acquiring route
returns a real reusable binding/rebill identifier. It never derives a
saved card token from transient tokenization tokens, bank customer IDs,
masked PANs, or Sber/T-Bank-specific intermediate IDs.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes a saved-card credential for the supplied merchant customer.
Future card-on-file charges using this `card_token_id` will be rejected.

parameters.description: Saved card token returned by card setup.
parameters.name: card_token_id

parameters.description: Merchant's stable customer identifier used when the card was saved.
parameters.name: customer_id

404.description: Saved card token not found for this tenant/customer

post.description:
Creates a Hosted Payment Page checkout session for redirect integrations.
The API key selects sandbox or live; this request does not accept an
`environment` field. `payment_methods` must come from
`GET /payment-methods/available` for the same key environment.

409.description: Idempotency conflict or invalid checkout state

post.description:
Replaces or creates products by SKU for the organization bound to the
secret API key. Use one idempotency key per catalog import batch.

parameters.description: Optional explicit organization guard. Must match the API key organization.
parameters.name: organization_id

parameters.description: Optional explicit organization guard. Must match the API key organization.
parameters.name: organization_id

post.description:
Creates a Foreign POS sale/cart for the organization bound to the secret
API key, prices it through the configured local-payment-settlement currency
chain, and returns the immutable pricing snapshot.

Use one idempotency key per merchant-side receipt/order. Retrying with
the same key returns the same sale and must not create a second payment.

post.summary: Create or retrieve an SBP QR for a Foreign POS sale

get.description:
Returns the Foreign POS capabilities for the organization bound to the
secret API key. Use this endpoint before creating sales to verify the
local currency, customer payment currency, merchant settlement currency,
and enabled payment methods.

parameters.description: Optional explicit organization guard. Must match the API key organization.
parameters.name: organization_id

get.summary: Get the Foreign POS store configuration

post.description:
Creates a hosted Arc Pay payment link. This endpoint requires a secret
API key and an `Idempotency-Key` header; never call it from browser code.
The selected payment method/mode pairs become the allowed methods
shown on the hosted payment page.

`redirect_url` is one merchant return URL for all hosted link outcomes.
Confirm success, failure, cancellation, pending 3DS, refund, or void
through webhooks or payment lookup.

400.description: Missing idempotency key or malformed request

409.description: Idempotency conflict or invalid link state

delete.description:
Cancels an active link for the authenticated tenant. Existing payments keep
their own payment lifecycle; canceling a link only prevents new buyer
starts from that hosted URL.

409.description: Link cannot be canceled from its current state

get.description:
Returns the current link configuration and lifecycle state for the
authenticated tenant. Use this for one-time, reusable, invoice, and
recurring links before showing update/cancel actions in your back office.

Returns the method/mode pairs that the authenticated merchant can use in
the requested environment. This is the public discovery endpoint for
deciding whether to show an H2H card form, redirect checkout, SBP, or a
bank wallet option.

Environment is selected by the API key. The `environment` query parameter
is an explicit guard: it must match the key environment (`sk_test_*` /
`pk_test_*` -> `sandbox`, `sk_live_*` / `pk_live_*` -> `live`) or the API
returns `400 api_key_env_mismatch`.

The response is scoped to the merchant's active shop configuration for
that environment. Currency, country, amount, and terminal-specific limits
are advertised when available and always validated when creating a
payment, checkout session, or link; do not render methods that are absent
from this list.

Sandbox method availability is per merchant/terminal and the response is
the source of truth for the API key. The standard public card-only lab can
expose only `bank_card + redirect` and `bank_card + h2h`; SBP, SberPay,
TPay, AlfaPay, Dolyami, Mir Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and BNPL require
explicit sandbox enablement or terminal assignment before testing.

Returns tenant-scoped payments for the authenticated secret key. Use this
endpoint for reconciliation dashboards, order lookup, and polling when a
webhook has not arrived yet.

Results are sorted by `created_at` descending. `date_from` is inclusive,
`date_to` is exclusive, both are interpreted as UTC RFC3339 timestamps,
and the filter is applied to `created_at`. Capture, refund, and settlement
time filtering belongs to reporting/settlement exports, not this
operational payment lookup endpoint.

post.description:
Creates a draft payment and returns `status=created`. Bank execution is a
separate step:

- H2H/custom form: tokenize card data with the browser-safe publishable
  key, then call `/payments/{id}/execute` from the merchant backend with a
  secret key.
- Hosted Payment Page / redirect flows: create a payment link or HPP
  session; the HPP service executes the payment after the buyer chooses a
  method.

If `callback_url` is provided, Arc Pay sends a dynamic callback for this
payment. Active portal webhook endpoints subscribed to the event can also
receive the payment event. Omitting `callback_url` disables only the
payment-specific dynamic callback; it does not disable portal webhook
delivery.

The API key selects sandbox or live; this request does not accept an
`environment` field. Use `GET /payment-methods/available` with the matching
key environment before rendering methods, then treat creation as the final
validation point for currency, amount, terminal, and bank constraints.

Creates and immediately executes a merchant-initiated card-on-file charge
using a saved `card_token_id` created by `POST /cards/setup`. The token is
scoped to the authenticated tenant and the supplied `customer_id`.

This is the public REST surface for the existing card-on-file payment
service contract. It does not collect PAN/CVV and does not expose card
data to the merchant.

A reusable `card_token_id` is returned only after the selected bank
terminal returns a real reusable binding/rebill identifier. Arc Pay does
not synthesize saved-card tokens from transient H2H tokenization tokens,
masked PANs, bank customer identifiers, or successful payments that did
not create a reusable binding.

404.description: Saved card token not found for this tenant/customer

post.description:
Captures funds for an AUTHORIZED payment. Partial capture supported —
remaining amount is automatically voided.

After the merchant frontend loads the 3DS Method URL in a hidden iframe
(device fingerprinting), it notifies this endpoint with the completion
indicator. This advances the 3DS 2.x flow so the ACS can make a
frictionless/challenge decision with enriched device data.
Requires a secret API key (sk_*), so the browser must call the merchant
backend first; do not expose `sk_*` to browser JavaScript.

parameters.description:
Client-generated UUID request key. Required for consistency with
mutating H2H operations and request tracing. 3DS Method completion is
deduplicated by Arc Pay's payment-scoped active `three_ds` operation;
duplicate browser retries while that operation is active do not call
the bank again.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

200.description: Method completion result; may contain ACS challenge redirect

post.description:
Executes an existing payment using the selected `payment_method` and
`payment_mode: h2h`. For `bank_card`, pass the `card_token_id` returned
by `/tokenize` plus `browser_info` for 3DS. For wallet/APM methods such
as `sbp` and `sberpay`, pass `wallet_interaction`; Arc Pay returns a typed
`wallet_action` that the merchant-hosted form or SDK renders.

Arc Pay maps the method/mode pair to the internal route configured for
the merchant's shop and initiates the bank authorization. May return
immediately (authorized/captured/failed), require card browser handoff
through `next_action`, or require wallet handoff through `wallet_action`.
Requires a secret API key (sk_*).

Browser SDK integrations should use the standardized
`confirmPayment()`/`handleNextAction()` helpers instead of building a
bank-specific 3DS state machine. Raw REST integrations should follow the
same contract: branch only on `next_action.type`,
`next_action.three_ds.phase`, `wallet_action.action`, and Arc Pay
payment statuses.

3DS branch rules:

- If `next_action.type=three_ds_method`, render the returned hidden form
  in an iframe. After it completes or times out, your backend calls the
  `completion_endpoint` with `three_ds_server_trans_id`.
- If `next_action.type=three_ds_challenge`, render the returned visible
  browser POST form. Arc Pay standardizes 3DS 1.x and 2.x into the same
  `submit` object, so integrations do not branch on bank-specific fields.
- After ACS completion, rely on webhook delivery and `GET /payments/{id}`
  for final state. Treat challenge timeouts as pending until the payment
  reaches a terminal status or `timeout` and reconciliation completes.
- Terminal payment statuses are `authorized`, `captured`, `settled`,
  `voided`, `expired`, `refunded`, `chargeback`, `declined`, and
  `failed`. `timeout` is not terminal.
- If Arc Pay returns `504` with `error.code=timeout`, the bank route did
  not answer before the public API deadline. Keep the order pending and
  poll or wait for a webhook; do not classify this as `technical_error`
  or retry with a new idempotency key.

429.description:
Request capacity exceeded. The response includes `Retry-After`;
retry the same payment after the indicated interval.

get.description:
Returns normalized bank/OFD fiscal receipt status and result data for a
payment. `payload` and `error` contain bank-specific fields returned by
the acquiring receipt-status API; stable fields such as `status`,
`receipt_id`, and `ofd_receipt_url` are surfaced separately.
Fiscal receipt registration is asynchronous on bank/OFD side. For Sber,
`getReceiptStatus` should be polled no earlier than 6 minutes after the
payment operation. If the bank/OFD provider has no receipt status for a
fiscalized payment, this endpoint returns `409` with
`error.code=fiscal_receipts_unavailable`.

409.description: Receipts are not available for this payment or adapter

get.summary: Get fiscal receipts for a payment

post.description:
Creates a refund for a CAPTURED or SETTLED payment. Partial refunds supported.
Total refunded amount must not exceed captured amount.

409.description: Payment not in refundable status or total refund exceeds captured

post.description:
Accepts card data from the buyer browser, validates it, forwards it to
card-service for tokenization, and returns an opaque `card_token_id`. The
token is valid for 5 minutes and single-use.

Prefer JS SDK Hosted Fields for custom checkout pages: Arc Pay iframes
collect PAN, expiry, and CVV, while your page receives only validation
state and the tokenization result. If you build your own raw-card form,
your environment handles cardholder data and must be prepared for the
applicable PCI DSS controls before live traffic.

Requires a publishable API key (`pk_*`) in `Authorization: Bearer` or
`X-Api-Key`. CVV is never stored by Arc Pay; it transits in memory only.

409.description: Payment not in created state or wrong payment method

Cannot void captured or settled payments — use refund instead.

payment.authorized.description:
Emitted when the issuing bank approves the auth-hold on the
cardholder's funds. Funds are reserved but not yet captured.
Two-stage payments stay in AUTHORIZED until your capture call;
one-stage flows transition immediately to CAPTURED (you may
receive both events back-to-back).

bank_auth_code.description: Issuer authorization code for the original payment.

bank_internal_ref.description: Bank/acquirer internal reference for dispute matching.

bank_rrn.description: Retrieval Reference Number from the card network or bank registry.

payment.captured.description:
Emitted when the captured amount has been debited from the cardholder.
For one-stage payments this fires after a successful auth without a
separate capture call.

bank_auth_code.description: Issuer authorization code for the original payment.

bank_internal_ref.description: Bank/acquirer internal reference for dispute matching.

bank_rrn.description: Retrieval Reference Number from the card network or bank registry.

payment.chargeback.description:
Cardholder filed a dispute with their issuing bank. The disputed
amount is held from the next settlement until the dispute is
resolved. Worst-case dispute windows vary by network and reason code:
Visa and Mastercard can reach 540 days for some delayed-delivery or
services-not-received scenarios; Mir card disputes can reach 360 days;
SBP dispute handling can reach 540 days. See the Arc Pay chargeback
policy documentation for merchant-facing operating guidance.

payment.created.description:
Emitted when a payment record is first created via POST /payments,
before any bank interaction. The payment is in CREATED state.

payment.declined.description:
Bank-side decline (do_not_honor, insufficient_funds, restricted_card,
fraud_suspected, expired_card, etc.) or AML rule decline. The decline
reason is in `payment.decline_code`. Terminal — re-attempt requires a
new payment with a new idempotency key.

payment.expired.description:
Authorization-hold timed out before a capture was issued. Typical
auth window is 7 days; varies per bank. Funds are returned to the
cardholder automatically — no merchant action required.

payment.failed.description:
Internal or upstream error preventing the payment from completing.
Distinct from declined — failed indicates Arc Pay or the bank could
not reach a definitive decision before final timeout. Terminal.

payment.refunded.description:
Funds returned to the cardholder. Partial refunds are supported up
to the captured amount; this event fires once per refund operation,
not once per payment. payment.captured_amount and payment.refunded_amount
update accordingly.

payment.settled.description:
Emitted when a captured payment is included in a settlement batch.
This is an operations/accounting signal, not a buyer-facing payment result.

payment.timeout.description:
Bank did not respond within Arc Pay's outbound timeout window. NOT
a terminal state — the bank may still confirm asynchronously, in
which case payment.captured or payment.failed follows. Do NOT
cancel the order on timeout.

payment.voided.description:
Authorization-hold released without capture, typically because the
merchant called POST /payments/{id}/void before capture, or
partial capture left a remainder that auto-voids.
